title: 2002 HMMT February Guts Problem 29
statement: A sequence \(s_{0}, s_{1}, s_{2}, s_{3}, \ldots\) is defined by \(s_{0}=s_{1}=1\) and, for every positive integer \(n, s_{2 n}=s_{n}, s_{4 n+1}=s_{2 n+1}, s_{4 n-1}=s_{2 n-1}+s_{2 n-1}^{2} / s_{n-1}\). What is the value of \(s_{1000}\) ?

solutions.text: 720 Some experimentation with small values may suggest that \(s_{n}=k\) !, where \(k\) is the number of ones in the binary representation of \(n\), and this formula is in fact provable by a straightforward induction. Since \(1000_{10}=1111101000_{2}\), with six ones, \(s_{1000}=6!=720\).
